item.title: Teen diver wins bronze for Fiji
item.description: Maori Pomeroy Farrell, a 17-year-old little-known aquatic diver, has put Fiji on the global map at the World Junior Diving Championships in Croatia. Maori, who has links to Dama village in Bua and Levuka Vakaviti in Ovalau, claimed a bronze medal at in the Boys’ 3-metre springboard event, finished third with a total score of 490.50 points, to claim a bronze medal at the event.
item.content:encoded:
Maori Pomeroy Farrell, a 17-year-old little-known aquatic diver, has put Fiji on the global map at the World Junior Diving Championships in Croatia.

Maori, who has links to Dama village in Bua and Levuka Vakaviti in Ovalau, claimed a bronze medal at in the Boys’ 3-metre springboard event, finished third with a total score of 490.50 points, to claim a bronze medal at the event.

It is the first-ever medal won by Fiji at an aquatic world meet.

Germany’s Finn Awe won gold with 560.60 points, while Matvei Pomoshnikov of Russia took silver with 542.00 points.

World Aquatics said in a short post on the achievement on their social media platforms “Maori Pomeroy-Farrell claims bronze at the , becoming the first-ever Fijian athlete to win a medal at a World Aquatics competition. A landmark moment for Fiji diving and a huge achievement on the world stage.”

Maori held off challengers from Mexico, Lithuania, Germany and the United States to clinch the bronze medal.

The teenager is also scheduled to compete in the boys’ under-18s one metre dive.

His dad Dan Farrell said the family are proud of Maori’s achievement and believe his strong performance has now put Fiji on the world map in the sport.

“Maori charged through a field of 43 international competitors, entering the 12-man final in 12th position.

“Then he turned it up a notch, fighting like a Fijian warrior and charging all the way to bronze, channeling the strength of his vanua, from Dama, Bua, to Levuka, Ovalau, his vuvale and all of Fiji stand proudly with him as he makes history for his nation on the world stage.”

Maori, whose family had to relocate from Canada to Mexico so that he could train and compete in the sport he now loves, is the first to represent Fiji in the sport at the world meet.

His participation in Croatia has been funded by the Fiji Sports Commission.

item.title: Defending champion faces tough BOG test
item.description: With the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants just eight days away, defending champion Labasa FC will enter the tournament under the spotlight, with coach Alvin Chand preparing his side for another demanding title campaign. The tournament kicks off next Friday at Four R Stadium, Govind Park, in Ba, where Chand will begin his quest to guide the Babasiga Lions to back-to-back BOG titles.
item.content:encoded:
With the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants just eight days away, defending champion Labasa FC will enter the tournament under the spotlight, with coach Alvin Chand preparing his side for another demanding title campaign.

The tournament kicks off next Friday at Four R Stadium, Govind Park, in Ba, where Chand will begin his quest to guide the Babasiga Lions to back-to-back BOG titles.

Chand’s journey with Labasa Football has been built over almost a decade.

After joining the district setup around 2016, he spent several years working with the youth teams before progressing into senior football.

His promotion to head coach in March, 2025, replacing Ravneel Pratap, marked the beginning of a breakthrough season.

Chand immediately made his mark, guiding Labasa to the 2025 BiC Fiji FACT title before securing the Extra BOG crown with a 2-1 victory over Rewa in the final at Subrail Park.

This year, however, the challenge will be greater.

As defending champion, Labasa will be one of the teams every opponent wants to beat.

The Babasiga Lions have been drawn in a competitive pool alongside Nasinu, Suva and Navua, setting up three important matches during the opening weekend.

For Chand, retaining the title would cap a remarkable rise through the Labasa system and strengthen his reputation as one of Fiji’s emerging football coaches.

With the countdown now underway, the pressure is on the champions to prove they can do it again.

item.title: Tui Suva Trophy set for Hibiscus clash
item.description: The Tui Suva Trophy will take place next Wednesday, bringing Suvavou Rugby Club and Vatuwaqa Rugby Club together in a traditional clash that signals the start of the Hibiscus Festival celebrations. Held the week of the Hibiscus Festival events, the fixture has become a regular part of the lead-up, giving supporters an early taste of the excitement surrounding the annual celebration.
item.content:encoded:
The Tui Suva Trophy will take place next Wednesday, bringing Suvavou Rugby Club and Vatuwaqa Rugby Club together in a traditional clash that signals the start of the Hibiscus Festival celebrations.

Held the week of the Hibiscus Festival events, the fixture has become a regular part of the lead-up, giving supporters an early taste of the excitement surrounding the annual celebration.

Vatuwaqa has dominated the recent rivalry, winning the Tui Suva Trophy in the past two years.

Suvavou will be determined to end that run when the two sides meet next week, while Vatuwaqa will be aiming for a third consecutive victory.

The match carries significance for both clubs, with players competing not only for the trophy but also for community pride.

The annual contest brings together supporters from the two Suva communities and provides an opportunity for the clubs to showcase their rugby in front of their fans.

For Suvavou, the target will be to reclaim the trophy, while Vatuwaqa will look to maintain its recent hold on the silverware.

With the Hibiscus Festival following, the Tui Suva Trophy promises to provide an exciting opening to the celebrations and set the tone for the week ahead.

item.title: Two sports, one dream
item.description: SEVENTEEN-YEAR-OLD Neumi Nanuku is making a name for himself in two different sports, dividing his time between football and rugby, but it is rugby that holds a special place in his heart. The Ba Sangam College student has built a promising sporting path through football and rugby sevens, taking every opportunity to test himself and pursue his dream of representing Fiji one day.
item.content:encoded:
SEVENTEEN-YEAR-OLD Neumi Nanuku is making a name for himself in two different sports, dividing his time between football and rugby, but it is rugby that holds a special place in his heart.

The Ba Sangam College student has built a promising sporting path through football and rugby sevens, taking every opportunity to test himself and pursue his dream of representing Fiji one day.

Nanuku plays midfield for Ba Sangam in football and recently helped the school win the under-17 title at the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship.

Just a week before that triumph, he was in Wallis and Futuna playing at first five-eighth for the U18 Nawaka rugby sevens team, where they made it all the way to the final. The quick change from rugby to football was demanding, but Nanuku embraced it.

His return from Wallis and Futuna came at a crucial time for Ba Sangam, with the national school’s championship approaching. Despite having little time to settle back into his routine, he joined his schoolmates and played his part in a successful campaign.

For Nanuku, the two sports offer different challenges and help him develop as an athlete.

Football has given him an opportunity to improve his awareness, movement and understanding of the game, while rugby remains the sport closest to his heart.

Although he enjoys playing football, Nanuku hopes his future will eventually lead him towards the Fiji rugby team.

At the same time, he has not closed the door on football and dreams of one day representing Fiji in either sport.

That ambition is what keeps him working.

At 17, he knows there is still plenty to learn, but his recent experiences have given him confidence that he can compete at a higher level.

His rugby sevens trip to Wallis and Futuna was another important step, allowing him to experience playing outside Fiji and measure himself against new opposition.

His success with Ba Sangam soon after showed his ability to adapt and stay focused despite the demands of a busy sporting schedule.

Nanuku also carries a familiar name in Fiji rugby.

He is the namesake of former Fiji national sevens player Neumi Nanuku, giving him a special connection to the sport he hopes to pursue.

But the teenager from Burenitu, Nalawa, Ra, is determined to create his own identity rather than simply live under a famous name.

His journey is still beginning, and there are many decisions ahead.

For now, he is focused on improving his game, balancing his studies at Ba Sangam and making the most of every opportunity that comes his way.

Whether his pathway eventually leads through rugby or football, the goal remains the same, to wear the Fiji jersey one day.

And with his versatility, ambition and willingness to take on new challenges, Nanuku is already taking the first steps towards that dream.

item.title: Basketball teams set for showdown
item.description: THE Fiji Secondary Schools basketball championship takes centre stage today as teams prepare for a three-day battle for honours from August 27-29. The championship will bring together young basketballers from schools across the country, with teams looking to make their mark from the opening day and build momentum towards later stages.
item.content:encoded:
THE Fiji Secondary Schools basketball championship takes centre stage today as teams prepare for a three-day battle for honours from August 27-29.

The championship will bring together young basketballers from schools across the country, with teams looking to make their mark from the opening day and build momentum towards later stages.

Defending champion for the under-19 boys and U17 girls last year, Yat Sen Secondary School will enter the tournament with pressure of being the team to beat but will need to maintain their composure and consistency if they are to retain the crown. The championship will also provide a platform for young basketballers to showcase their skills, represent their schools and gain valuable experience in a competitive environment. The tournament will feature more than 20 schools over three days.

item.title: BOG fever
item.description: Preparations are gathering pace for the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament, with Fiji Football Association chief executive officer Mohammed Yusuf confident fans will be treated to another exciting football spectacle when the competition kicks off next Friday. The tournament will be staged at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, in Ba from September 4 to 6, with the country’s top districts battling for one
item.content:encoded:
Preparations are gathering pace for the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament, with Fiji Football Association chief executive officer Mohammed Yusuf confident fans will be treated to another exciting football spectacle when the competition kicks off next Friday.

The tournament will be staged at 4R Stadium, Govind Park, in Ba from September 4 to 6, with the country’s top districts battling for one of Fiji football’s most coveted titles.

Yusuf said most participating teams had used the two-week break to prepare intensively for the tournament, while Rewa had benefited from additional match exposure through its Extra Premier League commitments following its OFC Champions League campaign.

“Preparations are well underway for the Extra Battle of the Giants tournament in Ba next week. Majority of the participating teams have been on a two week break and they have been preparing intensively for the event. Rewa is still completing its Extra Premier League matches after competing in the OFC Champions League so they are getting some good game time as well.”

Yusuf is also expecting strong support from football fans, recalling the atmosphere generated during last year’s Inter-District Championship in Ba.

“We all saw how it was in Ba during the IDC last year and we expect the same atmosphere when the tournament kicks off next week Friday.”

The opening day on September 4 features Ba against Nadi at 7.30pm, Rewa takes on Lautoka at 5pm, Labasa faces Nasinu at 3pm and Suva meets Navua at 1pm.

Yusuf confirmed ticket sales have already begun.

“Ticket sales have begun. We have set reasonable ticket prices for the separate seating and fans can check our social media pages as how they can purchase their tickets.”

item.title: Boselawa earns his Drua chance
item.description: Nadroga centre Kavekini Boselawa has earned a major opportunity to take the next step in his rugby career after signing as a Senior Development Player with the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua. Boselawa impressed new Drua head coach Brad Mooar and club officials during Round 1 of this year’s Skipper Cup competition in Lautoka, earning recognition for his physicality and versatility.
item.content:encoded:
Nadroga centre Kavekini Boselawa has earned a major opportunity to take the next step in his rugby career after signing as a Senior Development Player with the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua.

Boselawa impressed new Drua head coach Brad Mooar and club officials during Round 1 of this year’s Skipper Cup competition in Lautoka, earning recognition for his physicality and versatility.

The signing reflects the Drua’s commitment to creating pathways for talented local players to progress towards Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific.

Boselawa, who hails from Naduri in Macuata and has maternal ties to Nadrala in Nadroga, is a latecomer to rugby. He played soccer throughout his primary and secondary school years before taking up rugby at 19 while studying Land Surveying at Fiji National University.

He quickly made an impression with Nadrala Rugby Club and Nadroga, establishing himself as a promising centre.

“I am happy and quite emotional and thank the Lord for this opportunity,” Boselawa said.

He credited his father, who played in the outside back and midfield positions, as his biggest influence.

“My Tou has had the biggest influence on me, as a man and on my rugby journey,” he said.

Boselawa said he was looking forward to the opportunity to play in front of his family and the Drua’s passionate home supporters.

Mooar said Boselawa immediately stood out when he watched him play in Lautoka and praised his attributes as a back.

“Kavekini immediately stood out when I watched him in Lautoka,” Mooar said.

item.title: Marama Cup race intensifies in round five
item.description: THE battle for Marama Cup honours continues this week with Round 5 featuring six provincial clashes as teams look to strengthen their campaigns. Malolo will host Ba in one of the round’s fixtures, while Kadavu faces Lautoka in another contest between sides looking to make their mark.
item.content:encoded:
THE battle for Marama Cup honours continues this week with Round 5 featuring six provincial clashes as teams look to strengthen their campaigns.

Malolo will host Ba in one of the round’s fixtures, while Kadavu faces Lautoka in another contest between sides looking to make their mark.

Western rivals Nadroga and Navosa will meet, while Suva goes up against Rewa in a match that promises plenty of competition.

The remaining fixtures will see Nadi take on Taveuni and Tailevu face Naitasiri.

With the competition now entering its fifth round, teams will be looking to turn their performances into consistent results as the race for the top positions develops.

The coming round will be particularly important for teams aiming to stay within reach of the leading pack, with every result becoming increasingly valuable as the season progresses.

With six matches on the programme, round 5 provides another opportunity for players to showcase their talent and for teams to strengthen their claims for a place among the leading contenders.
